templates.name: generative-art-feedback
templates.description: Generative art feedback loop: noiseTOP seeds a feedback system. The feedbackTOP accumulates frames, transformTOP warps the output, and compositeTOP blends the original noise with the warped feedback. Fans out: noiseTOP drives BOTH feedbackTOP (input 0) AND compositeTOP (input 1).

operators.label: Noise Source
operators.purpose: Generates the initial noise texture that seeds the feedback loop

operators.label: Feedback Accumulator
operators.purpose: Accumulates frames from the transform chain, creating temporal smearing.

operators.label: Warp Transform
operators.purpose: Rotates, scales, and translates the feedback output each frame

operators.label: Mix Blend
operators.purpose: Blends the original noise (input 0) with the warped feedback (input 1)

operators.label: OUT
operators.purpose: Rendered output for display or downstream processing

connections.note: noiseTOP output → feedbackTOP input 0: seeds the feedback accumulator
feedbackTOP → transformTOP input 0: accumulated frames get warped each tick
transformTOP → compositeTOP input 0: warped feedback is the main input
noiseTOP → compositeTOP input 1: original noise mixed with feedback (fan-out)
compositeTOP → nullTOP input 0: final blended output

parameters.note: Simplex noise gives organic, flowing shapes for feedback art
Target TOP set to transform so loop picks up warped output
Subtle 1° rotation per frame creates spiral motion
Slight zoom-in each frame compresses the feedback
Feedback at 85% opacity to avoid runaway brightness
Original noise at 25% as subtle texture

templates.pythonBuilder:
# generative-art-feedback
# Builds: noiseTOP → feedbackTOP → transformTOP → compositeTOP → nullTOP
def build_generative_art_feedback(parent):
    parent = op(parent)
    noise = parent.create(noiseTOP, 'noise_src')
    noise.par.type = 'simplex'
    noise.par.resolutionw = 512
    noise.par.resolutionh = 512
    feedback = parent.create(feedbackTOP, 'feedback')
    feedback.inputConnectors[0].connect(noise)
    feedback.par.reset = 'resetnone'
    transform = parent.create(transformTOP, 'transform')
    transform.inputConnectors[0].connect(feedback)
    transform.par.rotate = 1.0
    transform.par.scale1 = 0.99
    transform.par.scale2 = 0.99
    feedback.par.targettop = transform.name
    composite = parent.create(compositeTOP, 'composite')
    composite.inputConnectors[0].connect(transform)
    composite.inputConnectors[1].connect(noise)
    composite.par.operand = 'add'
    composite.par.scale1 = 0.85
    composite.par.scale2 = 0.25
    output = parent.create(nullTOP, 'OUT')
    output.inputConnectors[0].connect(composite)
    noise.nodeX = -300; noise.nodeY = 0
    feedback.nodeX = 0;   feedback.nodeY = 0
    transform.nodeX = 300;  transform.nodeY = 0
    composite.nodeX = 600;  composite.nodeY = 0
    output.nodeX = 900;    output.nodeY = 0
    return output
build_generative_art_feedback('/project1')

templates.name: audio-reactive-spectrum
templates.description: Audio-reactive spectrum visualizer: audiofileinCHOP feeds an FFT audiospectrumCHOP, mathCHOP applies gain, and choptoTOP converts the spectrum to a texture for rendering.

operators.label: Audio Source
operators.purpose: Loads and plays an audio file as a CHOP channel stream

operators.label: FFT Spectrum
operators.purpose: Performs real-time FFT analysis, outputting frequency magnitude channels

operators.label: Gain + Post-Process
operators.purpose: Amplifies and optionally smooths the spectrum channels

operators.label: Spectrum Texture
operators.purpose: Converts CHOP channels to a 1D texture (one row per channel sample)

operators.label: OUT
operators.purpose: Final spectrum texture for display or GLSL sampling

connections.note: audiofileinCHOP → audiospectrumCHOP input 0: audio channels fed to FFT
audiospectrumCHOP → mathCHOP input 0: frequency magnitudes post-processed
mathCHOP → choptoTOP input 0: processed channels mapped to pixel rows
choptoTOP → nullTOP input 0: final spectrum texture

parameters.note: 512-sample FFT window balances frequency resolution and latency
10× gain to make quiet frequencies visible
Rows layout: each CHOP channel becomes a texture row

templates.pythonBuilder:
# audio-reactive-spectrum
# Builds: audiofileinCHOP → audiospectrumCHOP → mathCHOP → choptoTOP → nullTOP
def build_audio_spectrum(parent, audio_path=''):
    parent = op(parent)
    audio_in = parent.create(audiofileinCHOP, 'audio_in')
    if audio_path:
        audio_in.par.file = audio_path
    audio_in.par.play = 1
    spectrum = parent.create(audiospectrumCHOP, 'spectrum')
    spectrum.inputConnectors[0].connect(audio_in)
    spectrum.par.fftsize = 512
    spectrum.par.outputmenu = 'setmanually'
    spectrum.par.outlength = 256
    spectrum.par.timeslice = True
    math = parent.create(mathCHOP, 'math')
    math.inputConnectors[0].connect(spectrum)
    math.par.gain = 10
    chop_to_top = parent.create(choptoTOP, 'chop_to_top')
    chop_to_top.inputConnectors[0].connect(math)
    chop_to_top.par.dataformat = 'r'
    chop_to_top.par.layout = 'rowscropped'
    output = parent.create(nullTOP, 'OUT')
    output.inputConnectors[0].connect(chop_to_top)
    audio_in.nodeX = -600; audio_in.nodeY = 0
    spectrum.nodeX = -300; spectrum.nodeY = 0
    math.nodeX = 0; math.nodeY = 0
    chop_to_top.nodeX = 300; chop_to_top.nodeY = 0
    output.nodeX = 600; output.nodeY = 0
    return output
build_audio_spectrum('/project1', '/path/to/audio.wav')

templates.name: particle-system-basic
templates.description: Basic POP particle system with feedback loop: spherePOP emits particles, particlePOP simulates them, noisePOP adds turbulence, trailPOP draws trails, renderPOP converts to texture, and a nullPOP serves as the feedback target.

operators.label: Source Points
operators.purpose: Generates initial particle positions on a sphere surface

operators.label: Particle Sim
operators.purpose: Core particle solver: simulates physics, births particles, manages lifecycle.

operators.label: Turbulence Force
operators.purpose: Applies curl/random noise force to particles for organic motion

operators.label: Trails
operators.purpose: Records particle history as connected trail segments

operators.label: Render to TOP
operators.purpose: Converts the POP point cloud into a rendered texture

operators.label: Feedback Target
operators.purpose: Stores the previous frame's particle state for the solver feedback loop.

operators.label: OUT
operators.purpose: Final rendered texture for display or compositing

connections.note: spherePOP → particlePOP input 0: initial point positions seed the solver
particlePOP → noisePOP input 0: solved positions get turbulence applied
noisePOP → trailPOP input 0: jittered points generate trails
trailPOP → nullPOP input 0: trail output becomes the feedback target.
trailPOP → renderPOP input 0: trail geometry rendered to texture
renderPOP → nullTOP input 0: final rendered texture

parameters.note: Points to null_fb — this closes the solver feedback loop.
Noise amplitude — controls how chaotic the motion is
Noise frequency — spatial scale of turbulence

templates.pythonBuilder:
# particle-system-basic
# Builds: spherePOP → particlePOP → noisePOP → trailPOP → (nullPOP + renderPOP) → nullTOP
def build_particle_system(parent):
    parent = op(parent)
    sphere = parent.create(spherePOP, 'sphere')
    sphere.par.radx = 1.0
    sphere.par.rady = 1.0
    sphere.par.radz = 1.0
    particle = parent.create(particlePOP, 'particle')
    particle.inputConnectors[0].connect(sphere)
    particle.par.birthrate = 100
    particle.par.lifeexpect = 3
    particle.par.enabletimeintegration = True
    noise_force = parent.create(noisePOP, 'noise_force')
    noise_force.inputConnectors[0].connect(particle)
    noise_force.par.amp0 = 0.5
    noise_force.par.freq0 = 2.0
    trail = parent.create(trailPOP, 'trail')
    trail.inputConnectors[0].connect(noise_force)
    trail.par.length = 10
    null_fb = parent.create(nullPOP, 'null_fb')
    null_fb.inputConnectors[0].connect(trail)
    particle.par.particlesupdatepop = null_fb.name
    render = parent.create(renderPOP, 'render')
    render.inputConnectors[0].connect(trail)
    output = parent.create(nullTOP, 'OUT')
    output.inputConnectors[0].connect(render)
    sphere.nodeX = -900; sphere.nodeY = 0
    particle.nodeX = -600; particle.nodeY = 0
    noise_force.nodeX = -300; noise_force.nodeY = 0
    trail.nodeX = 0; trail.nodeY = 0
    null_fb.nodeX = 0; null_fb.nodeY = -150
    render.nodeX = 300; render.nodeY = 0
    output.nodeX = 600; output.nodeY = 0
    return output
build_particle_system('/project1')

templates.name: glow-bloom
templates.description: Classic glow/bloom post-processing effect: source TOP feeds a levelTOP (thresholds highlights), blurTOP spreads the bright areas, and compositeTOP additively blends the blurred glow back over the original.

operators.label: Source
operators.purpose: Input video or image that will receive the glow effect

operators.label: High-Pass Threshold
operators.purpose: Crush blacks so only bright highlight areas pass through

operators.label: Glow Blur
operators.purpose: Gaussian blur spreads the isolated highlights into a soft glow

operators.label: Add Blend
operators.purpose: Additively composites the blurred glow (input 1) over the original source (input 0)

operators.label: OUT
operators.purpose: Final glow-enhanced output

connections.note: source → levelTOP input 0: original image enters high-pass chain
levelTOP → blurTOP input 0: isolated highlights get blurred
source → compositeTOP input 0: original image is the base layer (fan-out)
blurTOP → compositeTOP input 1: blurred glow overlaid on base layer
compositeTOP → nullTOP input 0: final blended output

parameters.note: Operate on luminance not individual RGB channels

templates.pythonBuilder:
# glow-bloom
# Builds: source → levelTOP → blurTOP → compositeTOP (blend with original) → nullTOP
def build_glow_bloom(parent, source_path=''):
    parent = op(parent)
    source = parent.create(moviefileinTOP, 'source')
    if source_path:
        source.par.file = source_path
    level = parent.create(levelTOP, 'level')
    level.inputConnectors[0].connect(source)
    level.par.blacklevel = 0.6
    level.par.luminance = True
    blur = parent.create(blurTOP, 'blur')
    blur.inputConnectors[0].connect(level)
    blur.par.filtertype = 'gaussian'
    blur.par.size = 3
    composite = parent.create(compositeTOP, 'composite')
    composite.inputConnectors[0].connect(source)
    composite.inputConnectors[1].connect(blur)
    composite.par.operand = 'add'
    output = parent.create(nullTOP, 'OUT')
    output.inputConnectors[0].connect(composite)
    source.nodeX = -600; source.nodeY = 0
    level.nodeX = -600; level.nodeY = -150
    blur.nodeX = -300; blur.nodeY = -150
    composite.nodeX = 0; composite.nodeY = 0
    output.nodeX = 300; output.nodeY = 0
    return output
build_glow_bloom('/project1')

templates.name: glsl-shader-pipeline
templates.description: GLSL shader with multi-input uniforms: constantTOP provides a time uniform (input 0), noiseTOP provides a procedural texture (input 1), and glslTOP applies a custom fragment shader combining both.

operators.label: Time Uniform
operators.purpose: Provides a time-varying RGBA float uniform for use as u_Time in the GLSL shader.

operators.label: Procedural Texture
operators.purpose: Generates a procedural noise texture used as a shader input sampler

operators.label: GLSL Fragment Shader
operators.purpose: Runs a custom fragment shader with two inputs

operators.label: OUT
operators.purpose: Final shader output for display

connections.note: constantTOP → glslTOP input 0: time uniform accessible as uInput1
noiseTOP → glslTOP input 1: procedural texture accessible as sTD2DInputs[1]
glslTOP → nullTOP input 0: rendered shader output

parameters.note: RGBA 32-bit float for precise time channels
Simplex noise gives smooth, organic patterns
Force shader recompile when parameters change

templates.pythonBuilder:
# glsl-shader-pipeline
# Builds: constantTOP(time) → glslTOP(input 0) + noiseTOP → glslTOP(input 1) → nullTOP
def build_glsl_shader(parent):
    parent = op(parent)
    time_uniform = parent.create(constantTOP, 'time_uniform')
    time_uniform.par.format = 'rgba32float'
    time_uniform.par.resolutionw = 1
    time_uniform.par.resolutionh = 1
    time_uniform.par.value0r.expr = 'absTime.frame'
    texture_input = parent.create(noiseTOP, 'texture_input')
    texture_input.par.type = 'simplex'
    texture_input.par.resolutionw = 512
    texture_input.par.resolutionh = 512
    glsl = parent.create(glslTOP, 'glsl')
    glsl.inputConnectors[0].connect(time_uniform)
    glsl.inputConnectors[1].connect(texture_input)
    glsl.par.refreshpulse = 1
    glsl.par.resx = 512
    glsl.par.resy = 512
    output = parent.create(nullTOP, 'OUT')
    output.inputConnectors[0].connect(glsl)
    time_uniform.nodeX = -600; time_uniform.nodeY = -150
    texture_input.nodeX = -600; texture_input.nodeY = 150
    glsl.nodeX = 0; glsl.nodeY = 0
    output.nodeX = 300; output.nodeY = 0
    return output
build_glsl_shader('/project1')

templates.name: chroma-key-composite
templates.description: Chroma-key compositing pipeline: foreground source → chromakeyTOP removes a color, then overTOP composites the keyed foreground (input 1) over a background source (input 0).

operators.label: Foreground (Greenscreen)
operators.purpose: Foreground video footage shot against a green or blue screen

operators.label: Background
operators.purpose: Background image/video that replaces the keyed-out color

operators.label: Chroma Key
operators.purpose: Removes the specified chroma color from the foreground

operators.label: Over Composite
operators.purpose: Composites the keyed foreground (input 1) over the background (input 0)

operators.label: OUT
operators.purpose: Final composited output

connections.note: foreground → chromakeyTOP input 0: video to be keyed
background → overTOP input 0: base/background layer
chromakeyTOP → overTOP input 1: keyed foreground overlaid on background
overTOP → nullTOP input 0: final composite

templates.pythonBuilder:
# chroma-key-composite
# Builds: fg → chromakeyTOP, bg → overTOP(input 0), chromakey → overTOP(input 1) → nullTOP
def build_chromakey(parent, fg_path='', bg_path=''):
    parent = op(parent)
    fg_source = parent.create(moviefileinTOP, 'fg_source')
    if fg_path:
        fg_source.par.file = fg_path
    bg_source = parent.create(rampTOP, 'bg_source')
    bg_source.par.phaser.expr = 'absTime.frame * 0.01'
    chromakey = parent.create(chromakeyTOP, 'chromakey')
    chromakey.inputConnectors[0].connect(fg_source)
    chromakey.par.keycolorr = 0.0
    chromakey.par.keycolorg = 1.0
    chromakey.par.keycolorb = 0.0
    chromakey.par.thresholdr = 0.4
    chromakey.par.thresholdg = 0.4
    chromakey.par.thresholdb = 0.4
    chromakey.par.spillthreshold = 0.2
    over = parent.create(overTOP, 'over')
    over.inputConnectors[0].connect(bg_source)
    over.inputConnectors[1].connect(chromakey)
    over.par.outputresolution = 'input1'
    output = parent.create(nullTOP, 'OUT')
    output.inputConnectors[0].connect(over)
    bg_source.nodeX = -600; bg_source.nodeY = -150
    fg_source.nodeX = -600; fg_source.nodeY = 150
    chromakey.nodeX = -300; chromakey.nodeY = 150
    over.nodeX = 0; over.nodeY = 0
    output.nodeX = 300; output.nodeY = 0
    return output
build_chromakey('/project1')

templates.name: kaleidoscope
templates.description: Kaleidoscope effect chain: noiseTOP generates a source pattern, transformTOP rotates/scales the input, and kaleidoscopeTOP applies radial mirroring.

operators.label: Source Pattern
operators.purpose: Generates a procedural noise texture as the kaleidoscope seed

operators.label: Rotate & Scale
operators.purpose: Animates rotation and scale to create dynamic kaleidoscope motion

operators.label: Kaleidoscope
operators.purpose: Applies radial segment mirroring with configurable segment count

operators.label: OUT
operators.purpose: Final kaleidoscopic output

connections.note: noiseTOP → transformTOP input 0: source pattern enters the transform
transformTOP → kaleidoscopeTOP input 0: transformed image enters the kaleidoscope
kaleidoscopeTOP → nullTOP input 0: final mirrored output

parameters.note: Simplex noise produces smooth, organic patterns
Square resolution ensures symmetric kaleidoscope segments
8 radial segments — powers of two give clean symmetry

templates.pythonBuilder:
# kaleidoscope
# Builds: noiseTOP → transformTOP → kaleidoscopeTOP → nullTOP
def build_kaleidoscope(parent):
    parent = op(parent)
    source = parent.create(noiseTOP, 'source')
    source.par.type = 'simplex'
    source.par.resolutionw = 512
    source.par.resolutionh = 512
    transform = parent.create(transformTOP, 'transform')
    transform.inputConnectors[0].connect(source)
    transform.par.rotate.expr = 'absTime.frame * 1.5'
    transform.par.scale1 = 1.01
    transform.par.scale2 = 1.01
    kaleido = parent.create(kaleidoscopeTOP, 'kaleido')
    kaleido.inputConnectors[0].connect(transform)
    kaleido.par.segments = 8
    output = parent.create(nullTOP, 'OUT')
    output.inputConnectors[0].connect(kaleido)
    source.nodeX = -600; source.nodeY = 0
    transform.nodeX = -300; transform.nodeY = 0
    kaleido.nodeX = 0; kaleido.nodeY = 0
    output.nodeX = 300; output.nodeY = 0
    return output
build_kaleidoscope('/project1')

templates.name: edge-detect
templates.description: Edge detection with composite blending: source TOP → edgeTOP extracts edges, blurTOP softens the edge lines, and compositeTOP blends the softened edges (input 1) over the original source (input 0).

operators.label: Source
operators.purpose: Input texture for edge detection

operators.label: Edge Detect
operators.purpose: Sobel-based edge detection — outputs a grayscale edge map

operators.label: Soften Edges
operators.purpose: Softens the raw edge map so the composite blend looks painterly

operators.label: Edge Blend
operators.purpose: Composites softened edges (input 1) additively over original source (input 0)

operators.label: OUT
operators.purpose: Final edge-enhanced output

connections.note: source → edgeTOP input 0: original image enters edge detection
edgeTOP → blurTOP input 0: raw edges get softened
source → compositeTOP input 0: original image as base layer (fan-out)
blurTOP → compositeTOP input 1: softened edges overlaid
compositeTOP → nullTOP input 0: final edge-enhanced result

parameters.note: Sobel edge detection gives clean, directional edges
Gaussian blur for even edge softening
1-pixel blur — just enough to soften harsh edges
Additive blend so edges brighten the source
Edges at 50% opacity for subtle illustrative effect

templates.pythonBuilder:
# edge-detect
# Builds: source → edgeTOP → blurTOP → compositeTOP (blend with original) → nullTOP
def build_edge_detect(parent):
    parent = op(parent)
    source = parent.create(noiseTOP, 'source')
    source.par.type = 'simplex'
    source.par.resolutionw = 512
    source.par.resolutionh = 512
    edge = parent.create(edgeTOP, 'edge')
    edge.inputConnectors[0].connect(source)
    edge.par.type = 'sobel'
    edge.par.strength = 0.5
    blur = parent.create(blurTOP, 'blur')
    blur.inputConnectors[0].connect(edge)
    blur.par.filtertype = 'gaussian'
    blur.par.size = 1
    composite = parent.create(compositeTOP, 'composite')
    composite.inputConnectors[0].connect(source)
    composite.inputConnectors[1].connect(blur)
    composite.par.operand = 'add'
    composite.par.scale2 = 0.5
    output = parent.create(nullTOP, 'OUT')
    output.inputConnectors[0].connect(composite)
    source.nodeX = -600; source.nodeY = 0
    edge.nodeX = -600; edge.nodeY = -150
    blur.nodeX = -300; blur.nodeY = -150
    composite.nodeX = 0; composite.nodeY = 0
    output.nodeX = 300; output.nodeY = 0
    return output
build_edge_detect('/project1')
